summary: Facepalm: I ran out of search capacity early, after only a handful of broad searches, and found one candidate that just meets the rules. A third-party mailing sent Lynchburg, Va., absentee ballot applications with the wrong return PO box and ZIP code. It has one accepted news source (WSET, Oct. 19) plus the city registrar's own notice (lynchburgva.gov, Oct. 16). It's a weak candidate: nobody has named the mailer, so the subject is "unnamed", and it's another election-mail story after a week of them, though it would be a new state (VA). Other leads failed for lack of accepted sources: Deschutes County, Ore. (only KTVZ), and Texas's new 15,000-record voter backlog (only Votebeat, and I couldn't search for a second outlet). Genius: Genius scan for 2026-10-20 (window Oct. 14–20). No candidate met the two-source rule before the search limit ran out. The strongest lead was Google Quantum AI's magic state cultivation result on its Willow chip (Science, about Oct. 16). It is US-based and inside the window, but the only accepted page that opened was Phys.org (Oct. 17). The Science DOI page could not be reached, Scientific American's URL was not allowed, and every other outlet that covered it is outside the accepted list. Several ScienceDaily items dated Oct. 18–20 turned out to be reposts of studies from July and September. Nothing submitted for this side today. Pair published.

candidates.headline: University of Washington team uses AI to design protein-cutting enzymes from scratch
Third-party mailing sends Lynchburg, Va., absentee ballot applications with the wrong return PO box
Deschutes County, Ore., misspells a commission candidate's name in the voters' pamphlet and sends about 200 Bend voters the wrong precinct ballots
candidates.reason: In the window (Oct. 20), but the only news coverage found was KTVZ, Cascade Business News and The Source, none of which is on the accepted list. An official county page alone isn't enough.

candidates.headline: Texas Secretary of State's office sends counties 15,000 backlogged address-update records days before early voting
candidates.reason: In the window (Oct. 15–16), but Votebeat was the only accepted source found. Search capacity ran out before I could find a second publisher, and it's a follow-on to the earlier state registration error.

candidates.headline: Commanders coach Dan Quinn appears to lose track of downs on Monday Night Football
candidates.reason: Only one source (Fox News/OutKick), which frames it as disputed ('he has an explanation'). It's an on-field coaching call, not a clear self-evident blunder.

candidates.headline: Cambridge, Mass., voters warned about a mail-in ballot error
candidates.reason: The only coverage found was Patch, which isn't on the accepted list, and the nature of the error wasn't clear from the results.

candidates.headline: Japan's weather agency sends a false magnitude 9.9 earthquake alert
Google Quantum AI demonstrates magic state cultivation on Willow, cutting errors 40-fold (Science)
candidates.reason: Inside the window (Science, about Oct. 16) and US-based, but only one accepted source opened: Phys.org, Oct. 17. The Science DOI page was not accessible and Scientific American's page could not be fetched. Other coverage (The Quantum Insider, eWeek, Digitimes, Interesting Engineering, ScienceAlert, Google's blog) is not accepted. Worth retrying if a second accepted page turns up.

candidates.headline: University of Kentucky team restores two hours of sleep in Alzheimer's mice by depleting microglia
candidates.reason: Too old. UK's own release is dated July 16, 2026, and ScienceDaily's Oct. 19 page is a repost. It is also a mouse study.

candidates.headline: WashU team blocks CXCR3 to limit T-cell entry and neurodegeneration in tauopathy mice (Neuron)
candidates.reason: Too old. WashU Medicine's release is dated Sept. 28, 2026, and ScienceDaily's Oct. 20 page is a repost. It is also a mouse study.

candidates.headline: Van Andel-linked phase 2 trial suggests vitamin C may benefit people with pre-cancer blood disorders
candidates.reason: A hedged 'suggests / may benefit' result. The trial is largely Danish-led and the only accepted source is ScienceDaily.

candidates.headline: Europhysics Prize for the discovery of altermagnetism
candidates.reason: Not in the US. The prize was announced through Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz in Germany.

candidates.headline: Fujita Health University soy compound protects salt-fed mice from brain effects
candidates.reason: Not in the US (Japan). It is also a mouse study, and the original release dates to July.

candidates.headline: Year-long blind test of 12 methane-sensing satellites over Arizona (Nature)
candidates.reason: The only coverage opened was Nature's own summary, from the same publisher as the paper. The paper appears in the print issue (vol. 658), so the online date was not confirmed inside the window. It is also a validation study rather than a clear achievement.

candidates.headline: Gretchen Walsh breaks her own short-course 50m freestyle world record (22.75) in Charlottesville, Va. (Oct. 16)
candidates.reason: Still no accepted publisher. AFP's story appears only on France24 and Yahoo, and the rest of the coverage is Virginia Athletics, NBC Sports, SwimSwam and Swimming World.

candidates.headline: 13-year-old Raji Doshi of Farmington, Conn., named America's Top Young Scientist (Oct. 14)
candidates.reason: Still no accepted news publisher. The coverage found was 3M's release, Arizona Daily Sun, Yahoo, ISSA and other sites that are not accepted.

candidates.headline: 2026 Packard Fellowships for Science and Engineering announced (mid-October)
candidates.reason: Early-career research fellowships, closer to a funding award than a specific achievement. Only university and foundation pages were found, with no accepted news coverage.

candidates.headline: NASA's SPHEREx studies free-floating brown dwarfs (Space.com, Oct. 19)
candidates.reason: Only one accepted source (Space.com). The underlying paper and its date were not confirmed, and it is a survey result rather than a distinct first.
